title: Fix installation and simplify Outask documentation across platforms
scope: Fix the reproduced release-installer EACCES failure caused by an unrelated inaccessible PATH entry; add focused regression coverage; verify first install and command/MCP launch from a fresh supported shell without pre-seeding the command directory; clarify published macOS installation, permission failure handling, stable installed locations and Codex MCP registration in primary and packaged instructions. Preserve unrelated commands/data and explicit user-controlled client configuration. Do not claim the reported real-Mac incident is reproduced without its exact command/stderr; do not bypass sandbox or Gatekeeper restrictions, add project-local installation fallbacks, automatic client configuration or new CLI commands. Owner-authorized documentation correction now includes the full audited project documentation, generated target-specific README/help, corresponding focused checks and release-note validation. Continue in the same v1.1 candidate and preserve the owner's existing Mac test artifact. No remote push/publication authorization is inferred. Owner now explicitly approves one public root installer per destination: Linux install.sh, macOS Install.command, Windows Install.cmd. Move implementation helpers under app/scripts, invoke them directly, remove foreign-platform root launchers, and align help/docs/release notes/local helper/native acceptance. Migrate previous managed layouts without restoring obsolete installer files or deleting unrelated user files. Owner explicitly approves correcting first reads of genuinely uninitialised projects: list/count return empty/zero, consistent shared read APIs, without creating fake tasks/store files or masking missing configured/previously populated stores. Keep max page size 50 and existing safety boundaries; add regression coverage and deliver a fresh uniquely named Mac test archive. Owner now authorises correcting MCP parameter descriptions (ordinary cached-read defaults and page bounds) and preparing the v1.1 release PR under exact final remote-action agreement. Owner also explicitly requests removal of the old GitHub Release v1.0; preserve a local metadata/notes/assets backup and its Git tag. This specific deletion overrides the existing-release immutability rule only for that release.
acceptance: The actual release installer succeeds with a non-searchable unrelated PATH directory, and still refuses an accessible unrelated tasks command; a regression test fails against the original installer.

A native macOS archive acceptance starts with a fresh zsh HOME and PATH without the installed bin directory, runs the documented installer, discovers the installed tasks command in a new login shell and starts MCP by command name; Linux/Windows acceptance remains valid.

Project documentation follows the owner's approved concise command-first rewrite across all twelve Markdown files. README files remain under 200 lines; preserve unique shared contracts, safety/recovery and owner-controlled publication rules, fix contradictory read-side effects/source-only HTTP/release-default descriptions, and update live references together. Do not relocate unnecessary narrative into new files.
Independent review, focused QA and required local checks pass on the combined candidate; record concrete evidence and any still-unobserved real-Mac/Codex boundaries before candidate closure.

Include advancing stable version/lockfile and exact release notes under the project release value gate. Native hosted CI/archive gates require explicit remote-action agreement. Publication and downloaded-asset checks are read-only post-merge acceptance, never pre-merge claims.

The actual Linux x64, macOS arm64 and Windows x64 archives each contain short installation/use/MCP/update/uninstall instructions and installer help only for that archive's target platform. Windows distinguishes PowerShell/cmd.exe and its direct Node MCP launcher; POSIX recipes use the correct installed paths. Tests check executable commands, platform/runtime requirements and meaningful boundaries rather than explanatory paragraphs.

Remove the obsolete requirement to keep extracted downloads from the release-note policy, validator and future candidate notes together; preserve exact six-section notes, platform commands and all publication/recovery safeguards. Preserve the already handed-off Mac test artifact and create revised builds in a separate output directory.

Each actual archive has exactly one root installation entry: install.sh for Linux x64, Install.command for macOS arm64, Install.cmd for Windows x64. Installer implementation/helpers live under app/scripts; no other root install* or foreign-platform launchers remain. The target entry supports install/update/uninstall/help and preserves exit/error handling, dependency checks, ownership/collision protection and staged replacement.

Upgrading a previous managed archive layout removes obsolete managed root installer files while preserving unrelated/user files and project data. Tests cover real current archives, meaningful old-layout migration, failure paths and target-specific commands; source/local/native acceptance consumers and exact notes/recovery validation agree with the new layout. Preserve already handed-off archives and refresh independent review/QA.

On a genuinely uninitialised default project, shared reads return empty lists/search/batches or zero count; missing single IDs remain not found. Repeat/cache-bypassed reads do not materialise task/schema records or fake tasks. The first real create still works. Core/standalone, CLI, MCP and read-only HTTP agree at their public boundaries.

Keep errors for partial/previously populated/configured missing stores, malformed input/storage, permissions and pending recovery; do not silently repair or erase files. Preserve pagination max 50; count does not require pagination/projection parameters. Demonstrate meaningful regression failures before and passes after; refresh independent review/QA, then provide one current Mac test artifact in dist with a unique name and exact identity.

MCP tool metadata explicitly describes ordinary no_cache=false/omission with freshness-checked cache/JSON fallback, and limit 1–50/default 10 with pagination. All affected read tools agree; advertised machine schema and actual runtime defaults/bounds remain unchanged. Independent review and focused discovered-schema/runtime checks pass.

Prepare exact Outask AI v1.1 release notes, complete candidate closure and PR description after current origin/main integration and necessary local gates. Obtain one exact final push/draft PR/CI/ready agreement; leave owner-only merge/publication sequence intact. Complete explicitly requested v1.0 GitHub Release removal after preserving its exact metadata/notes/three assets locally and confirming v1.0 tag unchanged.

values.goal: Support reliable per-user installation and local CLI/MCP use on the declared platforms.
values.value: Users can install the release despite an unrelated inaccessible PATH entry and follow clear macOS/Codex setup instructions instead of an accidental project-local workaround. Readers can install, run and connect each supported target using concise commands, with shared contracts and delivery rules stated once.
values.observable_result: The reproduced installer failure is eliminated and a clean-shell installed-command/MCP scenario works at the user boundary. Project and generated documentation is short, consistent and specific to each build target.
values.verification: Run the regression against original/fixed installer, native distribution acceptance with a fresh shell PATH, and inspect the actual packaged instructions. Audit all documentation routes and compare the actual three archives/help with their platform's runnable recipes.
